LESSON: PEACEFUL CONFLICT RESOLUTION ● NEGOTIATION ● MEDIATION ● ARBITRATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.6: Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can resolving conflicts help us live peacefully in the community?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family
2. apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family
3. show empathy with survivors of conflicts in the family
4. appreciate the culture of peace in a society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PEACEFUL CONFLICT RESOLUTION ● NEGOTIATION ● MEDIATION ● ARBITRATION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: PEACEFUL CONFLICT RESOLUTION ● NEGOTIATION ● MEDIATION ● ARBITRATION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family

What this means
In this part you learn to identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family

What this means
In this part you learn to apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Show empathy with survivors of conflicts in the family

What this means
In this part you learn to show empathy with survivors of conflicts in the family. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show empathy with survivors of conflicts in the family.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show empathy with survivors of conflicts in the family. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the culture of peace in a society

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the culture of peace in a society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the culture of peace in a society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the culture of peace in a society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration. (skill: apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: show empathy with survivors of conflicts in the family)

Example 4: Connect “Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: appreciate the culture of peace in a society)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family.
3. Practise this skill: apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family.
4. Practise this skill: show empathy with survivors of conflicts in the family.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can resolving conflicts help us live peacefully in the community?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Peaceful Conflict Resolution ● Negotiation ● Mediation ● Arbitration means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family.
5. Be able to: apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
